newsitem.title: GERMANY: German defence lawyer calls for acquittal of Krenz.
newsitem.headline: German defence lawyer calls for acquittal of Krenz.

text.p: The defence lawyer for Egon Krenz, East Germany's last hardline communist leader, on Monday asked a Berlin court to acquit him on charges related to the Cold War killings of people trying to escape to the West.
"There can be no personal, individual blame for what happened at the border," lawyer Robert Unger said in his final statement.

Along with East Berlin Communist Party chief Guenter Schabowski and economic policy supremo Guenther Kleiber, Krenz is charged with three counts of manslaughter. Krenz alone faces a fourth manslaughter count.
But Unger argued that the Politburo executive body never issued border guards with an "order to shoot" fleeing East German citizens and that border policy was dictated by the former Soviet Union.
A final verdict is not expected before the end of August.
After the four-hour defence statement, the 60-year-old Krenz himself pleaded his innocence to the widow of a man killed attempting to cross the border.
"Never and not with a single word have I legitimised any deaths," he told her.
Given previous convictions of East German border guards and military leaders, "punishment is clearly unavoidable for Krenz," Unger conceded.

However Krenz's role in preventing a possible bloodbath as the Berlin Wall finally began to fall, by refusing to provide border guards with further arms, should be taken into account in his sentence, he argued.
State prosecutors last week demanded an 11-year jail sentence for Krenz, saying he bore direct responsibility for the killings as a member of the Politburo.

But the defence said any jail term should be substantially lower than the seven and half years already handed to the East German state Defence Minister Heinz Kessler, in a position of power for much longer than Krenz.

Krenz, who succeeded Erich Honecker as leader of the East German state as it began to crumble in 1989, has denied responsibility for the killings at the Berlin Wall, saying they were simply a product of the Cold War.
